business_rules: BR-01: TGO navigation must mirror the Trilogy platform structure and hierarchy (source: story description).
BR-02: Report navigation items must respect the existing report-permission model (report-permission changes already completed in a prior story).
BR-03: Admin-only navigation options must be visible only to authorized administrators (role-based visibility).
BR-04: Administrative and configuration options live in the right-side Settings menu, not the left navigation.
BR-05: Navigation behavior (expanded, collapsed, hover) must be consistent with the Trilogy platform reference screenshots.
functional_requirements: REQ-001: Reports remains available in the left navigation.
REQ-002: An Admin Reports submenu is displayed under Reports.
REQ-003: TGO Service Activity Report is displayed under Reports > Admin Reports.
REQ-004: The Service Activity Report navigation item respects the applicable report permissions.
REQ-005: Administrative and configuration options are available from the right-side Settings menu.
REQ-006: An Admin Config section is displayed in Settings.
REQ-007: Tenants is accessible through Settings > Admin Config > Tenants.
REQ-008: Sites is accessible through Settings > System > Sites.
REQ-009: Admin-only navigation options are visible only to authorized administrators.
REQ-012: Existing navigation functionality and authorized access continue to work without regression.
non_functional_requirements: REQ-010: The navigation works correctly in both expanded and collapsed states.
REQ-011: Hover navigation behaves consistently with the Trilogy platform.
dependencies: Report-permission changes for the TGO Service Activity Report (completed per story description).
Trilogy platform reference screenshots (5 attachments) define the expected structure — unreadable by this model run; saved to Downloads for human comparison.
Access to the Trilogy platform (or its screenshots) for side-by-side hover/structure comparison.
TGO QA test instance: https://trilogy-go-qa01.purplecheckpoint.com/tgo (from workflow config).
constraints: Role-based access and visibility must be preserved during the menu restructure.
Reports menu already exists; only the new hierarchy and moves are in scope.
assumptions: ASM-01: 'Administrative and configuration options' moved to Settings include at least Tenants (Admin Config) and Sites (System); the complete list of moved items is defined by the attached screenshots.
ASM-02: Users/roles exist in QA covering: full admin, user with Service Activity Report permission only, and user with no admin/report permissions.
ASM-03: The Settings menu is invoked from a right-side control (gear/avatar) consistent with Trilogy.

test_conditions.text: Reports item is present and functional in the left navigation.
Admin Reports submenu renders under Reports.
TGO Service Activity Report is reachable via Reports > Admin Reports.
Service Activity Report nav item is shown only with the applicable report permission and is enforced server-side.
Administrative/configuration options appear in the right-side Settings menu and no longer in their old locations.
Admin Config section renders inside Settings.
Tenants opens via Settings > Admin Config > Tenants.
Sites opens via Settings > System > Sites.
Admin-only options are visible/usable only by authorized administrators, in UI and on direct URL access.
All navigation paths work in expanded and collapsed states, including toggling between them.
Hover flyout/highlight behavior matches the Trilogy platform.
Pre-existing navigation items, routes, and role access are unchanged (regression).

coverage_criteria.target: All 12 acceptance criteria mapped to >=1 test case
REQ-004 and REQ-009 each have >=1 Positive and >=1 Negative case incl. direct-URL bypass
Expanded, collapsed, and expand<->collapse transition states each exercised
Admin / report-permission-only / no-permission roles each exercised against new menu items

coverage_considerations.reason: AC4 and AC9 are explicitly permission-based.

Menu labels are stated in ACs (Reports, Admin Reports, TGO Service Activity Report, Admin Config, Tenants, System, Sites); asserted in nav cases. Pixel-level layout requires the unreadable screenshots.
Navigation-structure story; no data create/update/delete in scope.
Direct-URL access bypassing hidden nav items must be rejected server-side.
No editable forms introduced by this story.
Navigation visibility changes; no auditable create/update/delete introduced. If unauthorized-access attempts should be logged, that is unspecified (see ambiguous requirements).
No shared-record editing in scope; menu is per-session UI state.
Refresh/deep-link of moved routes must be stable.
No list/search behavior changed by this story (report content itself is out of scope).
AC12 explicitly requires no regression to existing navigation and access.
No locale requirements stated for the menu; flagged as a gap if TGO is localized.
IDOR-style direct-URL access and session expiry mid-navigation.
Accessibility (keyboard), compatibility (browsers, viewport), usability (hover parity vs Trilogy).

missing_requirements: The complete list of 'administrative and configuration options' to be moved into Settings is defined only by the attached screenshots, which could not be read in this run — human must verify TC-007/TC-010 item lists against the attachments.
No AC states the expected behavior of the Admin Reports submenu when a user has no admin-report permissions (hidden vs. shown empty).
Supported browser matrix and minimum viewport width are not specified.
No AC covers mobile/tablet responsive behavior of the new menu (if in scope for TGO).

open_questions.question: When a user has no admin-report permission, is the Admin Reports submenu fully hidden or shown empty?
Which exact menu items (beyond Tenants and Sites) move to the Settings menu, and from which old locations are they removed?
What are the supported browsers and the minimum supported viewport width for the navigation?
Is Sites admin-only, or visible to non-admin roles under Settings > System?

exploratory_test_ideas: Explore the navigation with a user whose permissions are changed mid-session (permission revoked while menu already rendered) to discover stale-menu authorization gaps.
Explore hover/flyout behavior with browser zoom at 50%/200% to discover positioning and clipping defects.
Explore rapid expand/collapse toggling while a page is still loading to discover race conditions in nav state rendering.
Explore the Settings menu with a role that has exactly one admin permission (e.g. report-only) to discover partially-populated section rendering issues.
Explore keyboard + screen reader (NVDA) announcement of the new submenu hierarchy to discover accessibility regressions.
Explore direct navigation to legacy (pre-move) URLs of Tenants/Sites to discover broken bookmarks or missing redirects.
